text:
alex: Hey SREs — customer reporting intermittent 502s from our text-generation endpoint. They gave a request_id: 3a7f9b2e-0004 and a repro curl. Time window: 2026-03-15 09:12:00 -> 09:17:00 UTC. Region: us-west-2. Can someone look up server-side logs and say if this is a gateway timeout, upstream reset, or model OOM?

alex: Repro curl (customer says this reproduces reliably):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate" \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -H "X-Request-ID: 3a7f9b2e-0004" \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"short prompt to reproduce 502"}'
```

maria: Thanks Alex. Which service fronted the call? /v1/generate streaming or non-streaming? Any customer debug bundle or trace id? Also we need the exact node pool (prod vs canary) if they hit a dedicated route.

alex: Route was /v1/generate streaming (they used chunked transfer). Customer also supplied trace_id t-889abc in the payload. No debug bundle yet — asked them to hold while we fetch logs.

ingrid: I'll start a hot-shard search. Use this KQL to find related entries in Kibana (hot indices):
```
service.name: "api-frontend" and http.request.headers.x-request-id: "3a7f9b2e-0004"
```
If that returns nothing, run an archived search on cold storage with timestamp range. Example ES DSL (internal use):
```
GET /logs-*/_search
{
  "query": {
    "bool": {
      "must": [
        { "match_phrase": { "request_id": "3a7f9b2e-0004" }},
        { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "2026-03-15T09:12:00Z", "lte": "2026-03-15T09:17:00Z" }}}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

ingrid: Note retention: hot nodes keep full structured logs for 14 days by default; after that logs roll to cold (90d). If the customer time window is older than hot TTL we will need a cold-extract which can take ~30-90s to materialize.

ingrid: Also check pod logs on the model-serving pool (model-runner) for OOM or kv-cache errors. Example pod grep: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/model-runner --since=20m | grep 3a7f9b2e-0004`

alex: Got it. Can you also check the load balancer and upstream timeouts? The customer mentions latency spiking to ~800ms before the 502.

maria: On LB/frontdoor side, search access logs for 3a7f9b2e-0004 and check backend_status. KQL: `elb.request_id: "3a7f9b2e-0004"` or simply `http.response.status_code: 502 and http.request.headers.x-request-id: "3a7f9b2e-0004"`.

ingrid: I ran hot search and found frontend proxy entries but no model-runner logs in hot. Kicked off a cold extract for the model-runner shard and the archive query for the timeline you gave. Extraction job id: extract-20260315-7z. ETA ~45s.

logs-bot: Debug bundle requested by alex. Created bundle id: dbg-20260315-xy9. Contents: frontend logs, model-runner stderr/stdout, traces (trace t-889abc), and customer curl. Link: https://internal.redwood/debug/dbg-20260315-xy9 (internal only).

maria: Great — once cold extract finishes, please paste the matched log lines here. If we see repeated `upstream reset` or `connection reset by peer` from the model-runner, escalate to infra team for kernel/socket tracing. If we see GC/OOM, tag model-ops.

alex: I'll message the customer to ask for a reproduction toggle: please re-run the curl with an extra header `X-Include-Debug: true` so we can capture a richer debug bundle from the edge. Example: `-H \"X-Include-Debug: true\"`.

ingrid: Cold extract finished. Found model-runner stderr with this snippet: `2026-03-15T09:13:22Z ERROR model-runner: upstream write failed: write: connection reset by peer (request=3a7f9b2e-0004)` and a few `context deadline exceeded` entries in the proxy. Pasting minimal lines: 
```
2026-03-15T09:13:22.123Z ERROR model-runner request=3a7f9b2e-0004 msg="upstream write failed: connection reset by peer"
2026-03-15T09:13:22.124Z WARN  proxy request=3a7f9b2e-0004 msg="context deadline exceeded while waiting for model response"
```

maria: That looks like model-runner closed the socket. Ask model-ops to check kernel logs for `OOM-killer` or any segfaults around that timestamp on the runner nodes, and check if there were abrupt restarts.

alex: Noted. I'll open a quick internal incident for model-ops with bundle and logs. Customer update: "Thanks, please escalate — this is blocking production for us." I'll attach the debug bundle link.

ingrid: One more tip for future hunts: include both X-Request-ID and Traceparent header for distributed tracing. If we have traceparent we can tie spans across services faster.

maria: Filed model-ops ticket #INC-20260315-42 and assigned to @ingrid and @matt. Adding notes and attaching dbg-20260315-xy9. :thumbsup:

alex: Thanks team — will follow up after model-ops triage.
